finding.evidence: DB_PASSWORD, SMTP_PASSWORD and STRIPE_SECRET returned with HTTP 200
finding.description: Database, mail and payment secrets are public.

recommendation.goal: What is the recommended fix for this web security flaw: exposed-secrets (Database, mail and payment secrets are public. Evidence: DB_PASSWORD, SMTP_PASSWORD and STRIPE_SECRET returned with HTTP 200). State the concrete fix and cite a primary source (OWASP, MDN, NIST, PCI DSS, IETF RFC, or the vendor's own advisory).
recommendation.answer: Recommended fix for exposed DB_PASSWORD, SMTP_PASSWORD and STRIPE_SECRET returned with HTTP 200: immediately stop returning secrets in API responses. Remove those fields from the response body, enforce server-side field selection to control data exposure, keep Database, mail and payment secrets server-side only in env/vault, and rotate all exposed credentials. Per OWASP WSTG, APIs must not rely on client-side filtering.

verification.detail: This commonly happens when developers implement API endpoints by serializing entire backend objects (such as database models or internal data structures) directly into API responses, relying on the client-side code to filter out sensitive fields before presenting them to the user.
